contents: Displayed yield, actual good yield, and shop-floor defects did not agree, so measurement and decision reliability had to be checked before process settings. I led assembly-process trials and cross-team coordination, narrowing causes from measurement and sensors through inspection, jigs, consumables, and finally recipes. The team recorded 98.7% monthly average good yield in December 2024, and I directly revised the MSA criteria, SOP, QCP, P-FMEA, and inspection standards.

title: 2170 Assembly-Line Yield Stabilization

contents: Development was complete, but no equipment could run normally from start to finish, so production-start conditions were rechecked from an initial SAT-level baseline. I set the assembly trial direction and coordinated sensor, sequence, speed, alignment, punch-list actions, and retests across engineering, maintenance, and manufacturing. A representative automatic cycle was restored, and two 100-cell lots plus the final 50 cells were used as production-start evidence. Long-term production stability was separate.

The project advanced through A/B/C samples, about 20,000-cell trial production, and customer qualification and production approval in March 2025, but commercial production did not proceed because of pricing.

contents: A collector-based Tabless structure differed from the lead-tab process and could not be repeated without dedicated jigs and inspection methods. Five samples suitable for functional evaluation were secured from about 100 exploratory builds. Repeat production, manufacturability, and statistical superiority were not verified at this A-sample stage.

contents: Limited FAT samples and individual auto cycles could not prove end-to-end flow, repeatability, or readiness for actual production. I built acceptance sheets and punch lists, tracked supplier corrections and retests, and led actual cell production plus measurement and process-standard work. The team observed an initial snapshot of about 95% over roughly five days and 1,000 cells, including cells meeting criteria after rework, and documented FAT/SAT, MSA, and operating standards. It is not FPY or long-term production yield.

contents: The incumbent supplier could not cover the planned follow-on volume alone, so a new can supplier required manufacturing and quality validation. I translated material-property and bottom-geometry differences into beading, crimping, and sealing risks, then set the assembly conditions and validation sequence. After 600 cells across three lots and an official UN38.3 pass, purchasing and subsequent pilot production moved to the alternative can after existing stock was consumed.

contents: Manual shaping before pre-welding varied by operator and repeatedly created uncoated-edge damage and short-circuit risk. I separated the positive- and negative-electrode damage mechanisms, built a temporary jig, defined shape, position, and acceptance criteria, and ran sample and teardown tests. The condition was verified with about 400 samples, used in subsequent pilot production, and reflected in process/inspection standards, the P-FMEA, and production-equipment RFQ.

title: NCM Pre-Forming Process Validation

contents: Process-level MES data existed, but a cell's full history was not connected, so investigating ten customer-requested cells took about three days. After a MES enhancement request was rejected for cost, I spent about three weeks building Power Query consolidation and Excel VBA search and linking logic. A single search took 5–10 seconds and a ten-cell investigation about three minutes; the tool was used on site during my employment and handed over.

While performing overhaul and precision assembly, I documented parts, torque, alignment, leak, and repeatability checks in run sheets and SOPs and trained operators. Rework and overtime were observed to decrease, while team monthly output increased from 1–2 to 4–5 units during the same period.

A colleague handled recipe and bath analysis; I handled staged sample production and evaluation, inspection criteria, and customer-result feedback. The revised condition entered production and was monitored for about a year through the transition from legacy-condition parts.

contents: Stable internal results were insufficient when customer measurement methods and acceptance criteria differed. I rebuilt surface-treatment and inspection criteria, including Hi-Pot, acid resistance, and corrosion resistance, and supported same-sample correlation and technical audits. Repeated same-sample measurements identified differences in internal and customer equipment and decision methods, and the technical-qualification conditions were added to QCPs, run sheets, and inspection standards.

contents: Lab stripping was possible, but overlapping ultrasonic zones damaged the surface and left roughness, diffusion, and reusability risks unresolved. I documented sample and scale-up results and turned relative product/transducer movement, repeatability, and stopping criteria into pre-fabrication checks. Normal operation was not achieved; the case established that stripping feasibility and product reusability must be judged separately.

title: Diffuser Ultrasonic Stripping Scale-up Failure Analysis

contents: A model trained on public weld images lost substantial performance on practical specimens containing soot, spatter, reflections, and capture variation. I planned the overall project, compared candidate models and error images using recall and FPR, and owned low-resolution coordinate scaling and threshold FN/FP decisions. Recall on captured specimens rose from 15.84% to 85.15%, a gain of 69.31 percentage points, and the team completed a ResNet+DeiT and FastAPI/PWA inspection demo.

title: Building an AI Model to Find Defects in Welding Images

contents: JSON references had to survive exchanges between the PC and teaching pendant, while the robot command and status-monitoring paths needed one coherent flow. Future work can extend into long-duration E2E, recovery, Omniverse, and AI Teaching.

contents: Manufacturing, semiconductor, and battery knowledge accumulated with inconsistent terms and links, making evidence retrieval difficult. I structured the Markdown/YAML vault and link-graph index, then built a CLI that synchronizes changed files to ChromaDB and retrieves/reranks candidates. Markdown source management, incremental synchronization, candidate retrieval, and reranking are implemented. Source-location display, authorization, and repeated retrieval evaluation can extend it into an operating manufacturing-knowledge tool.
